listing_view.reasoning: Subscription climbed from ~1x on day one to nearly 62x by mid-day of the close date, which is a textbook frenzied final-day pattern and strongly indicates a listing pop, though the retail/QIB mix behind that number is unknown from what I was given. A 52x PE headline against a stated 128x 'industry average' also gives sellers a flattering cheapness story to market. I would temper this only because I have no anchor investor or grey market data, so my 80 rests heavily on one demand metric.

longterm_view.reasoning: The cash record is poor: operating cash flow was negative in two of the last three years and free cash flow was deeply negative (about -270, -997 million) before the latest year, meaning reported profits have not reliably converted into cash. Customer stickiness (top-ten relationships averaging over nine years [business, page 219]) is a genuine positive, but I was given no ROE, ROCE, debt or margin figures, so a price of 52x current earnings is unverifiable as value. Given thin evidence of durability plus proven cash burn, I lean modestly negative rather than neutral.

governance.reasoning: Nothing adverse surfaces in the extracts: no criminal proceedings against promoters and no SEBI disciplinary actions are disclosed [litigation, page 408][litigation, page 409], but ESOP grants at Rs 212.96 versus a Rs 272 cap price and disclosed related party transactions are normal-amber rather than clean-green. Score is near-neutral because the extracts are fragmentary.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Operating cash flow was negative in two of three years and cumulative free cash flow is deeply negative, so the earnings used to justify the PE may be lower quality than they appear.
The cheapness story rests entirely on a 128x peer average stated in the seller's own document, with zero peer rows independently verifiable from what I was given.
The prospectus references related party dealings including purchase of goods, which can obscure true margins and cash economics absent detail I was not given.
Repeated pledges of Rs 73-77 million against borrowings and guarantees signal leverage working alongside the negative free cash flow.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: Not answerable properly: the document states a 128.11x industry average PE but I was given zero parsed peer rows, so I cannot check who is in the set or whether outliers inflate the average. Be suspicious — a 128x 'average' is itself extreme, and being at 0.40x of an inflated benchmark proves nothing about being cheap. Treating 52x as a discount based on this figure alone would be trusting the seller's own yardstick.
answers.citation: not answerable from what I was given

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A clean peer table showing the 128x average is representative and genuinely comparable, plus three years of balance sheet and ROE/ROCE data showing the latest positive cash year is structural rather than a one-off, would move the long-term score up. Conversely, confirmation that the Rs 3,200 million fresh issue is paying down debt while promoters exit, or that the 62x subscription is almost entirely leveraged HNI flipping, would push the listing score down.
